subject: Architecture
title: Wind Tunnels Between Towers
description: Learn Wind Tunnels Between Towers in one minute.

hook.text: Some buildings create winds so strong that pedestrians get knocked off their feet.

buildup.text: Tall buildings funnel wind downward. Gaps between towers compress air into jet-like gusts.

discovery.text: The Bridgewater Place in Leeds created 80 mph gusts that flipped a truck and killed a pedestrian.

twist.text: Wind tunnel testing existed before these buildings. Some developers simply skipped the test.

climax.text: Cities now require wind studies for tall projects. Canopies and screens can tame the worst gusts.

punchline.text: The building looked great on paper. Nobody checked the wind.

quiz.question: What caused deadly wind gusts at Bridgewater Place?
options: The building's height funneled wind to street level
A gap in the facade created a whistling effect
